alternatives.argument: The rational-equivalence subgroup is generated by principal divisor cycles on integral subvarieties, using finite sums in the finite-type case and locally finite supporting families otherwise. On an affine chart of an integral supporting subvariety, write a rational function $a/b$ with $a,b$ nonzero. Its nonzero order can occur only at height-one primes containing $ab$. Such primes are minimal over $(ab)$, by the principal-ideal theorem in the domain, and there are finitely many because the ring is Noetherian. A finite affine cover gives global finiteness on a finite-type subvariety; otherwise it gives local finiteness. The local order function is already proved. On a normal subvariety its height-one local rings are DVRs, and the length order is exactly the ordinary Weil order. The quotient is therefore the stated Chow group. Top-dimensional cycles on an integral dimension-$n$ scheme give $A_n(X)=\mathbb Z[X]$, since no dimension-$(n+1)$ subvariety exists; cycles in greater dimensions vanish. The locally finite convention is essential for the non-quasi-compact operations. Stacks42.17/19 gives this exact definition; no unverified Fulton reading is used.

Define the classes by applying the operators of [[lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula]] to $[X]$ and use the operational-ring isomorphism in [[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]. Its projective bundle relation gives exactly the displayed relation and uniqueness. Normalization, arbitrary morphism naturality, rank vanishing, Whitney and the line-summand formula are already established for the operators; restriction under the operational isomorphism is the graph pullback, so these become the claimed ring identities. The regular-section formula follows from the supplier's projective-bundle induction and gives its zero-scheme fundamental cycle, with generic multiplicities. No assertion that arbitrary $f^*$ is injective is used; only flag/projective bundle pullback is injective.

Definitions via Chern roots, following Stacks, *Chow Homology*, Section 42.45 (tag 02UM, the Chern character and tensor products) and Section 42.65 (tag 02UN, Todd classes), and Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 6 (Chern classes) and 7 (the Todd class $T(X)$ of the tangent bundle, an element of $A(X)\otimes\mathbb Q$); the explicit expansions are Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 3.2.3 and Vakil 245 Class 18 Sections 2.1-2.2 (the definitions $\operatorname{ch}(E)=\sum e^{\alpha_i}$ and $\operatorname{td}(E)=\prod Q(\alpha_i)$, with $Q(x)=x/(1-e^{-x})$). Well-definedness of the expressions in the Chern classes is the splitting principle of [[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]]: any two filtrations with invertible quotients give the same symmetric expression because symmetric polynomials in the roots are the Chern classes; rational coefficients are needed for the exponential and the geometric expansions. The tangent bundle is locally free of rank $\dim X$ by [[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]].
Source status correction: Fulton was not retrieved/read and is a bibliographical comparison only. The proof prerequisites are the explicit local arguments and retrieved Stacks/Borel-Serre sources; any Vakil statement marked proof omitted is not accepted as proof evidence.

Compute, in order: (1) apply the projective bundle formula (thm-projective-bundle-formula-for-chow-groups) to the rank-$(n+1)$ free bundle on $\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose projectivization is $\mathbb P^n_k$, to get $A^*(\mathbb P^n_k)=\mathbb Z[\xi]/(\xi^{n+1})$ with $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$; set $h:=\xi$. (2) Identify the generators with linear subspaces: by induction on $d$, intersecting with a hyperplane $H\not\supseteq\Lambda$ of complementary position, the cap-action formula $c_1(\mathcal O(1))\cap[V]=[V\cap H]$ of def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class gives $h^d\cap[\mathbb P^n]=[\Lambda^{n-d}]$, so $A^d(\mathbb P^n)=\mathbb Z\cdot h^d$ corresponds to $A_{n-d}$; in particular $h^n=[\mathrm{pt}]$ with $\deg h^n=1$ (lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space fixes the degree isomorphism on $A_0$). (3) For hypersurfaces $H_i$ of degrees $d_i$, the class is $[H_i]=d_i h$ (def-degree-projective-hypersurface with the normalisation and additivity of $c_1$ from def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle and lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting), so $\deg([H_1]\cdots[H_n])=d_1\cdots d_n$. (4) State explicitly that this computes the product in the Chow ring; the identification with the cycle of the scheme-theoretic intersection is the proper-intersection/Tor-multiplicity statement, deliberately outside this page's scope.

Direct proof in four steps, all from scaffolded and published items. (1) Rational equivalence: $A_0(\mathbb P^2_k)\cong\mathbb Z$ is detected by degree (lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space), so the two $k$-rational points satisfy $[p]=[q]$; equivalently $[p]-[q]=\operatorname{div}(r)$ for the ratio $r$ of linear forms cutting the joining line. (2) Preimage cycles: $\pi^{-1}(p)=E\cong\mathbb P^1$ (thm-blowup-regular-surface-closed-point-regular, def-exceptional-divisor-blowup) and $\pi^{-1}(q)$ is the single reduced point $q'$ over $q\ne p$ (lem-blowup-isomorphism-off-center); the cycle of a preimage scheme is the corresponding basis class (lem-cycle-of-a-closed-subscheme). (3) Suppose the recipe were well defined on rational equivalence; then $[E]=[q']$ in $A_*(Y)$. The proper pushforward of lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined is well defined on rational equivalence and gives $\pi_*[E]=0$ (dimension drop $0<1$) and $\pi_*[q']=[q]$ (isomorphism over $q$, extension degree $1$), hence $[q]=0$, contradicting $\deg[q]=1$. (4) The hypotheses are sharp: pure fibre dimension fails exactly at $p$, so the flat case lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups does not apply, and the correct replacement is the refined Gysin construction of def-refined-gysin-pullback-for-regular-embeddings. State the AC inheritance from the blowup and Proj suppliers.

alternatives.argument: The rational-equivalence subgroup is generated by principal divisor cycles on integral subvarieties, using finite sums in the finite-type case and locally finite supporting families otherwise. On an affine chart of an integral supporting subvariety, write a rational function $a/b$ with $a,b$ nonzero. Its nonzero order can occur only at height-one primes containing $ab$. Such primes are minimal over $(ab)$, by the principal-ideal theorem in the domain, and there are finitely many because the ring is Noetherian. A finite affine cover gives global finiteness on a finite-type subvariety; otherwise it gives local finiteness. The local order function is already proved. On a normal subvariety its height-one local rings are DVRs, and the length order is exactly the ordinary Weil order. The quotient is therefore the stated Chow group. Top-dimensional cycles on an integral dimension-$n$ scheme give $A_n(X)=\mathbb Z[X]$, since no dimension-$(n+1)$ subvariety exists; cycles in greater dimensions vanish. The locally finite convention is essential for the non-quasi-compact operations. Stacks42.17/19 gives this exact definition; no unverified Fulton reading is used.

Define the classes by applying the operators of [[lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula]] to $[X]$ and use the operational-ring isomorphism in [[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]. Its projective bundle relation gives exactly the displayed relation and uniqueness. Normalization, arbitrary morphism naturality, rank vanishing, Whitney and the line-summand formula are already established for the operators; restriction under the operational isomorphism is the graph pullback, so these become the claimed ring identities. The regular-section formula follows from the supplier's projective-bundle induction and gives its zero-scheme fundamental cycle, with generic multiplicities. No assertion that arbitrary $f^*$ is injective is used; only flag/projective bundle pullback is injective.

Definitions via Chern roots, following Stacks, *Chow Homology*, Section 42.45 (tag 02UM, the Chern character and tensor products) and Section 42.65 (tag 02UN, Todd classes), and Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 6 (Chern classes) and 7 (the Todd class $T(X)$ of the tangent bundle, an element of $A(X)\otimes\mathbb Q$); the explicit expansions are Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 3.2.3 and Vakil 245 Class 18 Sections 2.1-2.2 (the definitions $\operatorname{ch}(E)=\sum e^{\alpha_i}$ and $\operatorname{td}(E)=\prod Q(\alpha_i)$, with $Q(x)=x/(1-e^{-x})$). Well-definedness of the expressions in the Chern classes is the splitting principle of [[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]]: any two filtrations with invertible quotients give the same symmetric expression because symmetric polynomials in the roots are the Chern classes; rational coefficients are needed for the exponential and the geometric expansions. The tangent bundle is locally free of rank $\dim X$ by [[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]].

Compute, in order: (1) apply the projective bundle formula (thm-projective-bundle-formula-for-chow-groups) to the rank-$(n+1)$ free bundle on $\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose projectivization is $\mathbb P^n_k$, to get $A^*(\mathbb P^n_k)=\mathbb Z[\xi]/(\xi^{n+1})$ with $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$; set $h:=\xi$. (2) Identify the generators with linear subspaces: by induction on $d$, intersecting with a hyperplane $H\not\supseteq\Lambda$ of complementary position, the cap-action formula $c_1(\mathcal O(1))\cap[V]=[V\cap H]$ of def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class gives $h^d\cap[\mathbb P^n]=[\Lambda^{n-d}]$, so $A^d(\mathbb P^n)=\mathbb Z\cdot h^d$ corresponds to $A_{n-d}$; in particular $h^n=[\mathrm{pt}]$ with $\deg h^n=1$ (lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space fixes the degree isomorphism on $A_0$). (3) For hypersurfaces $H_i$ of degrees $d_i$, the class is $[H_i]=d_i h$ (def-degree-projective-hypersurface with the normalisation and additivity of $c_1$ from def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle and lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting), so $\deg([H_1]\cdots[H_n])=d_1\cdots d_n$. (4) State explicitly that this computes the product in the Chow ring; the identification with the cycle of the scheme-theoretic intersection is the proper-intersection/Tor-multiplicity statement, deliberately outside this page's scope.

Direct proof in four steps, all from scaffolded and published items. (1) Rational equivalence: $A_0(\mathbb P^2_k)\cong\mathbb Z$ is detected by degree (lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space), so the two $k$-rational points satisfy $[p]=[q]$; equivalently $[p]-[q]=\operatorname{div}(r)$ for the ratio $r$ of linear forms cutting the joining line. (2) Preimage cycles: $\pi^{-1}(p)=E\cong\mathbb P^1$ (thm-blowup-regular-surface-closed-point-regular, def-exceptional-divisor-blowup) and $\pi^{-1}(q)$ is the single reduced point $q'$ over $q\ne p$ (lem-blowup-isomorphism-off-center); the cycle of a preimage scheme is the corresponding basis class (lem-cycle-of-a-closed-subscheme). (3) Suppose the recipe were well defined on rational equivalence; then $[E]=[q']$ in $A_*(Y)$. The proper pushforward of lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined is well defined on rational equivalence and gives $\pi_*[E]=0$ (dimension drop $0<1$) and $\pi_*[q']=[q]$ (isomorphism over $q$, extension degree $1$), hence $[q]=0$, contradicting $\deg[q]=1$. (4) The hypotheses are sharp: pure fibre dimension fails exactly at $p$, so the flat case lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups does not apply, and the correct replacement is the refined Gysin construction of def-refined-gysin-pullback-for-regular-embeddings.
